finding.claim: The /preview endpoint fetches a fully attacker-controlled URL server-side and returns the status code and the first 500 characters of the body. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), and localhost, and read the responses. requests follows redirects by default, which adds further reach.
finding.source: request.args.get('url') at app.py:15 (query parameter 'url' on GET /preview)
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) at app.py:16, with the response body returned at app.py:17

trace.note: Route /preview is registered with no authentication
target = request.args.get('url', '') takes the attacker-supplied URL
requests.get(target) is called directly with that URL
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned to the caller, so this is a non-blind SSRF

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, and redirects are not disabled. ALLOWED_HOSTS is not used on this route. The only control is timeout=5, which does not mitigate SSRF.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes request.args["url"] and app.py:16 passes it straight to requests.get with no scheme/host validation (the ALLOWED_HOSTS check exists only in /partner at app.py:23-25), and app.py:17 returns the status and the first 500 characters of the body.
